docs.title: Workflow for New Documents & Evolutionary Engine Hardening
docs.text: This document defines the standardized operational workflow when processing new historical books with AlexandriaSandwich and encountering novel typographic or layout anomalies.

docs.title: 1. The Core Paradigm
docs.text: The pipeline matures with each book. Scripts inside scripts/ are never duplicated or forked per job. Every edge-case fix and refinement flows directly into the central engine and automatically benefits all past and future books.

docs.title: Stage 1: Ingress & Baseline Run
docs.text:
1. Place scans in data/input/<job>/.
  2. Optionally specify book parameters in data/input/<job>/job.config.json.
  3. Execute standard pipeline: ./scripts/run_pipeline.sh --job <job>.

docs.title: Stage 2: Diagnostics & Edge-Case Inspection
docs.text: Inspect output artifacts in data/output/<job>/: - OCR pass rates and fallback costs (<job>.pipeline.json). - Textlayer alignment and drift (<job>.sandwich.pdf). - Layout structure in vector reprints (<job>.digital.pdf / <job>.typeset_edition.pdf).

docs.title: Stage 3: Generalized Solution in Core Engine
docs.text: Implement fixes strictly in scripts/: - Never branch on job name (if job == "xyz": ...). - Abstract structural features (e.g., column density, script/Unicode block, font scale differences).

docs.title: Stage 4: Regression Gate (Golden Master Guard)
docs.text: Run fast checks against reference jobs (alex_smoke, katha_06): - Ensure existing books suffer no quality regressions. - Validate that the new book succeeds and joins the verified reference fleet.

docs.text:
The system consists of three closely coupled containers:

cd /opt/alexandria

Create .env (file permissions 600):

# Optional: customize MISTRAL_API_KEY and paths

docker exec alexandria_worker typst --version

docs.title: 1. Production Architecture & Layout
docs.text:
The n8n instance runs on compute node alex.local alongside the alexandria_worker container:

Webhook → n8n ( Port 5678 )
       → /opt/alexandria/scripts/n8n_run_job.sh
       → docker exec alexandria_worker run_pipeline.sh
  • Trigger: Webhook requests are received and validated by n8n.
  • Execution: Via the host Docker socket, n8n invokes the job runner directly inside the isolated alexandria_worker container.
  • Response: Upon completion, the webhook synchronously returns the structured JSON execution report containing confidence scores and artifact paths.

docs.title: 📚 Pipeline Artifacts & Quality Status
docs.text:
The AlexandriaSandwich pipeline transforms historical print editions and manuscripts via a multi-stage hybrid workflow into various scholarly publication formats (facsimiles, sandwich PDFs, TEI-P5 XML, EPUB 3, and digital vector typeset editions).

This documentation page serves as the canonical reference for all generated artifacts, details their purpose, and documents the current quality and maturity levels of each stage to guide the continuous improvement process (CIP).

docs.title: 1. Processing Stages Overview
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[Raw Scans TIFF/PNG/PDF] --> B[Preprocessing: Deskew & Unpaper]
    B --> C[Tesseract HOCR & Quality Gate]
    C -->|Confidence < Threshold| D[Mistral Document OCR]
    C -->|Confidence >= Threshold| E[Consolidation]
    D --> E[Consolidation & book.json]
    E --> F1[Sandwich PDF & Aligned PDF]
    E --> F2[Typst Vector Typeset 1:1]
    E --> F3[TEI-P5 XML & EPUB 3]
    E --> F4[Audit Reports & Layout Checks]

docs.title: preprocessed/<job>/page_XXXX.png
docs.text:
• Path: data/processing/preprocessed/<job>/
  • Purpose: Prepares raw scans for OCR and facsimile generation via deskewing, unpaper border cleaning, gutter shadow suppression, and pure white leveling.
  • Quality Status:
  • Strengths: Highly uniform, clean white backgrounds; reliable separation of paper noise without clipping delicate diacritic marks (Anusvāra, ṛ, ḍ).
  • Challenges: Severe book spine gutter curvature limits linear deskewing; cylindrical warping correction is planned for extreme cases.

docs.title: page_XXXX.hocr & page_XXXX.json (Tesseract)
docs.text:
• Path: data/processing/qc/<job>/
  • Purpose: Fast local primary recognition at token and glyph level, producing geometric bounding boxes (bbox x0 y0 x1 y1) and confidence scores driving the quality gate.
  • Quality Status:
  • Strengths: Supplies exact coordinate geometry for every token detected on the original scan.
  • Challenges: Complex Indological scripts (IAST diacritics, Vedic accents, Devanagari) frequently fall below 85% confidence, creating corrupted text layers without fallbacks.

docs.title: page_XXXX.mistral.md & page_XXXX.mistral.json (Mistral Document OCR)
docs.text:
• Path: data/output/<job>/markdown/
  • Purpose: AI-powered fallback and high-fidelity transcription for pages failing the Tesseract gate, as well as complex tables, footnotes, and polytonic diacritics.
  • Quality Status:
  • Strengths: Near-flawless accuracy on IAST (ā, ī, ū, ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, ṃ, ḥ, ṅ, ñ, ṭ, ḍ, ṇ, ś, ṣ), Devanagari, and Vedic accents. Structural table parsing.
  • Challenges: Dense leader dot sequences in tables of contents may be rendered as raw punctuation runs. Standard Markdown omits per-token coordinate boxes.

docs.title: page_XXXX.sidecar.txt
docs.text:
• Path: data/output/<job>/
  • Purpose: Clean plaintext stream per page for external indexing (Elasticsearch, Solr) and command-line grep utilities.
  • Quality Status: Complete, fast, and directly synchronized with verified textual corpora.

docs.title: book.json (consolidate_book.py)
docs.text:
• Path: data/output/<job>/book.json
  • Purpose: Canonical single-source-of-truth data model unifying metadata, pagination, Tesseract coordinates, Mistral markdown, paragraph hierarchies, tables, and footnotes in a validated JSON schema.
  • Quality Status:
  • Strengths: Decouples ingestion from multi-format rendering; primary source for PDF, TEI, and EPUB export.
  • Challenges: Differentiating between running headers and opening body text occasionally requires page-level heuristics on heterogeneous prints.

docs.title: toc.json / toc.txt (inject_toc.py)
docs.text:
• Path: data/output/<job>/<job>.toc.txt (editable), data/output/<job>/toc.json
  • Purpose: Hierarchical table of contents tree with page mappings for automated injection of PDF bookmarks/outlines, PDF metadata, and authentic page labels (Roman for front matter, Arabic for main text).
  • TOC Outline & Quality Gate:
  • Automated Injection: All produced PDFs (facsimile, sandwich, vector typeset) are populated with bookmarks and page labels via inject_toc.py. The primary data source is an existing <job>.toc.txt (or <job>.toc.json), with an automatic fallback to chapter headings (h1/h2) extracted from book.json.
  • Validation & Normalization: Hierarchy levels are normalized automatically (starting at level 1 without skipped intermediate levels) to eliminate bookmark rendering errors.
  • Empty Outline Warning: If zero entries are detected, the gate logs a warning (Warning: Injected 0 hierarchical TOC entries); when --require-toc is set, the step exits with code 1.
  • Manual Editorial Control (.toc.txt): An accessible plain text file <job>.toc.txt is provided alongside the PDF (syntax: Title | PageNumber with 2 spaces indentation per level). Scholars can edit titles and page targets in any standard text editor and re-inject them losslessly within seconds using python3 scripts/inject_toc.py -i <pdf> --toc <job>.toc.txt.
  • Quality Status: Fully operational; provides standard accessible navigation across PDF viewers (Apple Preview, Acrobat, PDF.js) with 1:1 matching book page numbers.

docs.title: <job>.sandwich.pdf (assemble_sandwich.py)
docs.text:
• Path: data/output/<job>/<job>.sandwich.pdf
  • Purpose: Standard searchable PDF sandwich combining preprocessed page images with invisible Tesseract HOCR text layers.
  • Quality Status: Dependable for keyword search and basic copy-pasting; bounding boxes can drift slightly under damaged fonts.

docs.title: <job>.aligned.pdf (align_mistral_pdf.py)
docs.text:
• Path: data/output/<job>/<job>.aligned.pdf
  • Purpose: High-fidelity hybrid sandwich aligning high-accuracy Mistral OCR tokens to Tesseract bounding boxes via Dynamic Time Warping (DTW).
  • Quality Status:
  • Strengths: Highest text extraction fidelity in facsimile format; rare ligatures and complex diacritics select and copy reliably.
  • Challenges: Large tokenization discrepancies between engines require occasional fallback to line-level boxes.

docs.title: <job>.perfect_sandwich.pdf (build_perfect_sandwich.py)
docs.text:
• Path: data/output/<job>/<job>.perfect_sandwich.pdf
  • Purpose: Archival print-ready facsimile with adaptive contrast leveling, unsharp masking, content-aware margin masking (automated suppression of gutter shadows, binding strips, and scanning edges outside text boundaries), and invisible vector text layers (Render Mode 3).
  • Procedure (Content-Aware Margin Masking):
  • Dynamically extracts exact text bounding boxes per page from Mistral JSON geometry or word vectors.
  • Applies multiscale illumination background subtraction and leveling to pure white (#FFFFFF).
  • Masks contiguous gutter folds and scanner edges outside text boundaries (pad_x=75, pad_y=60) without clipping marginalia or page numbers.
  • Quality Status: Visually superior to raw archive scans; serves as the clean reference baseline for layout profiling and digital typesetting.

docs.title: layout.profile.json (profile_source_layout.py)
docs.text:
• Path: data/output/<job>/layout.profile.json
  • Purpose: Automated geometric profiling of the source facsimile (perfect_sandwich.pdf). Measures text column dimensions (Satzspiegel), page margins (top, bottom, inner, outer), leading/line spacing, macro layout structure (single-column, two-column, marginal sideheads), and header/folio coordinates.
  • Quality Status: Fully automated; feeds calibrated geometric parameters into the typesetting renderer.

docs.title: <job>.digital.typ & <job>.digital.pdf (render_digital_pdf.py)
docs.text:
• Path: data/output/<job>/<job>.digital.pdf
  • Purpose: Pure vector-based digital re-typesetting (not a raster image). Infinitely scalable, accessible, and rendered using authentic typefaces (Libertinus Serif, Noto Sans Devanagari).
  • Typographic Standards:
  • Satzspiegel & Spacing: Calibrated automatically from layout.profile.json and .perfect_sandwich.pdf.
  • Title & Paragraphs: Centered title block; structured first-line indentation (1.5em) on body text.
  • Header & Folio: Symmetrical three-column running headers with consistent Devanāgarī or Arabic page numbering.
  • Footnote Separation: Automated extraction and bottom-of-page formatting with hairline divider rules and reduced point sizes.
  • Modes:
  • 1:1 Original Page Correspondence (--preserve-pages): Every page starts on a new digital page matching original page numbers and headers, scaled adaptively via page_content to guarantee exact page parity.
  • Scholarly Reflow: Continuous re-typesetting with natural book breaks according to classical typographic proportions.
  • Quality Status:
  • Strengths: Razor-sharp typography, lightweight file size (200–800 KB vs. 20–50 MB for facsimiles), complete full-text accessibility.

docs.title: <job>.tei.xml (export_tei.py)
docs.text:
• Path: data/output/<job>/<job>.tei.xml
  • Purpose: TEI-P5 compliant XML export for Digital Humanities, computational linguistics, and long-term archival preservation according to Text Encoding Initiative standards.
  • Quality Status: Valid TEI-P5 with structured headers, divisions (<div>), paragraphs (<p>), and line breaks (<lb/>). Linguistic tagging can be added in downstream NLP pipelines.

docs.title: <job>.epub (export_epub.py)
docs.text:
• Path: data/output/<job>/<job>.epub
  • Purpose: Reflowable EPUB 3 e-book for mobile e-readers (Kindle, Apple Books, Kobo) with semantic XHTML5 markup.
  • Quality Status:
  • Strengths: Smooth reflow and customizable typography on handheld devices.
  • Challenges: Wide grammar tables (paradigms of declensions/conjugations) require specialized responsive CSS.

docs.title: <job>.report.md (generate_job_report.py)
docs.text:
• Path: data/output/<job>/<job>.report.md
  • Purpose: Automated end-of-run quality audit with pass/fail ratios, OCR confidence distributions, runtime metrics, and SHA-256 artifact checksums.
  • Quality Status: Serves as a deterministic gate in n8n pipelines and renders directly inside the web UI.

docs.title: <job>.layout_audit.json / <job>.layout_audit.md (audit_layout_concordance.py)
docs.text:
• Path: data/output/<job>/<job>.layout_audit.md, data/output/<job>/<job>.layout_audit.json
  • Purpose: Automated concordance gate comparing the cleaned facsimile (perfect_sandwich.pdf) against digital vector typesetting (digital.pdf). Computes fill ratio, whitespace divergence, structural zone concordance, horizontal center-of-mass, and Jaccard token overlap.
  • Quality Status: Indispensable automated layout gate.

docs.title: comparison_samples/ (compare_layout.py)
docs.text:
• Path: data/output/<job>/comparison_samples/page_XXXX_comparison.png
  • Purpose: Visual side-by-side verification images showing cleaned facsimile (left) versus digital typesetting (right) for instant inspection of Satzspiegel, line breaks, and page boundaries.
  • Quality Status: Generated automatically in every standard pipeline run.

docs.title: 1. The Target Structure: The 4-Tier Pyramid
docs.text:
In scientific digitization and scholarly editing, no single format satisfies all practical needs: - Facsimiles are essential for verification and citations, but useless on mobile e-readers (no reflow). - Reflowable text is ideal for mobile devices and AI, but loses the historical typographical layout. - XML ensures 50+ years of archival safety, but is difficult for humans to read casually.

AlexandriaSandwich resolves this dilemma with a 4-tier architecture where every book is transformed into a complementary set of digital formats:

              ┌───────────────────────────────────────┐
              │ 1. Reception Layer (End User)         │
              │    • EPUB 3 (Reflowable E-Reader)     │
              │    • Digital PDF (Typst Vector Reset) │
              └───────────────────▲───────────────────┘
                                  │ Compilation
              ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐
              │ 2. Working & AI Layer                 │
              │    • book.md (UTF-8 Plain Markdown)   │
              └───────────────────▲───────────────────┘
                                  │ Consolidation
              ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐
              │ 3. Semantic & Archival Layer          │
              │    • book.json (Single Source of Truth│
              │    • tei.xml   (TEI-P5 Academy Standard)
              └───────────────────▲───────────────────┘
                                  │ OCR & Token Alignment
              ┌───────────────────┴───────────────────┐
              │ 4. Facsimile & Proof Layer            │
              │    • <id>.sandwich.pdf (Scan + Layer) │
              │    • <id>.aligned.pdf  (AI-Aligned)   │
              └───────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: 1. Facsimile Layer: Sandwich PDF (*.sandwich.pdf / *.aligned.pdf)
docs.text:
• Role: Authentic, citable document archive.
  • Architecture:
  • Visual top: 300 DPI high-resolution facsimile scan with original letterpress fonts, marginalia, and layout.
  • Invisible bottom: Vector text layer with pixel-exact bounding-box coordinates for every word.
  • Post-Assembly Textlayer Correction (AI Alignment): The invisible text layer is synchronized with Mistral OCR. OCR errors and noise hallucinations (e.g. along dotted leader lines) are eliminated while preserving exact bounding box coordinates (*.aligned.pdf).

docs.title: 2. Machine-Readable Single Source of Truth: book.json (AST)
docs.text:
• Role: Central, software-agnostic intermediate format.
  • Architecture: Hierarchical Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) combining metadata, pages, paragraphs, headings, token lists, confidences, and bounding boxes ([ymin, xmin, ymax, xmax]).
  • Significance: From this file, any new target format (HTML, EPUB, Typst, LaTeX, SQL) can be compiled at any time without re-running OCR.

docs.title: 3. Scholarly Academy Standard: tei.xml (TEI-P5)
docs.text:
• Role: Long-term preservation (50+ years) and interoperability with academic repositories (DTA, SARIT, Perseus).
  • Architecture: Strictly valid TEI-P5 XML featuring <teiHeader>, facsimile mappings (<surface>, <zone>), and semantic structural divisions (<body>, <div n="..." type="...">, <p>, <table>).

docs.title: 4. Plain Text & AI Layer: book.md (UTF-8 Markdown)
docs.text:
• Role: Direct editing, version control, and LLM input.
  • Architecture: Clean UTF-8 Markdown without proprietary overhead.
  • Usage: Line-by-line versioning in Git (git diff), fast CLI inspection (grep), and optimal ingestion for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) vector stores.

docs.title: 5. Reader Reception Layer: *.epub (EPUB 3) & *.digital.pdf
docs.text:
• Role: Human reading experience on modern devices.
  • EPUB 3: Dynamic reflow for e-readers (Tolino, Kindle, Kobo, iPad) with embedded Unicode fonts for Devanagari (Noto Serif Devanagari) and IAST transliteration (Linux Libertine / Charis SIL).
  • Digital PDF (Typst): Crisp vector typesetting for print-on-demand or desktop study.

docs.title: 3. The Duality: Reproduce Original Layout vs. Complete Re-layout
docs.text:
By strictly separating image data, geometric coordinates, and semantic text, AlexandriaSandwich enables two complementary publication strategies:

                        ┌──────────────────┐
                        │ Raw Scan Source  │
                        └────────┬─────────┘
                                 │
                 ┌───────────────┴───────────────┐
                 ▼                               ▼
     [ STRATEGY 1: REPRODUCTION ]     [ STRATEGY 2: RE-LAYOUT ]
     • Pixel-exact Sandwich PDF       • Reflowable EPUB 3
     • Vector reset via bbox coords   • Responsive Web / HTML
     • Preserves historical fonts     • Study workbook format (Typst)
     • Page citations match original  • Variable font size & Dark Mode

docs.title: Strategy 1: Reproducing the Original Layout
docs.text:
1. As AI-Aligned Facsimile (*.aligned.pdf):
  2. The historical print layout is retained 1:1. Line breaks, hyphens, printer quirks, ligatures, and footnote placements remain identical to the physical library copy.
  3. As Geometric Vector Reset:
  4. Because book.json stores bounding boxes (bbox), line heights, and column widths, the original layout can be mathematically reconstructed in modern vector typesetting engines (identical page grid, but without scan noise).

docs.title: Strategy 2: Complete Re-layout of Content
docs.text:
1. Dynamic E-Reader Book (EPUB 3):
  2. Text flows freely. On small smartphone or tablet displays, margins, font sizes, and line spacing adapt dynamically to reader preferences.
  3. New Print Layouts (e.g. Student Workbook via Typst):
  4. Re-generate the entire work into an entirely different publication format:
    • Format shift (e.g. from historical Octavo to DIN A4 or ISO-B5).
    • Generous margins for handwritten student notes.
    • Modern typography (e.g. Linux Libertine O + Noto Serif Devanagari).
    • Bilingual parallel columns (Sanskrit on the left, German on the right).

docs.title: 4. Semantic Typesetting vs. Reverse-Layout Reconstruction (The Böhtlingk & Dhātupāṭha Model)
docs.text: Practical case studies (Böhtlingk 1887 and Dhātu-Pāṭha) establish a fundamental principle for the AlexandriaSandwich architecture:

docs.title: 4.1 Why Blind "Reverse-Layout" Fails
docs.text: Attempting to geometrically reconstruct the exact page layout of a complex historical work from raw, unsegmented OCR text produces severe typographical distortions: * Serialization Loss: OCR engines read multi-column reference tables (e.g., verbal roots on the left, meanings on the right) sequentially. 2D tabular alignments collapse into flat 1D paragraphs. * Layout Guesswork: Without a semantic model, Typst has to guess column breaks and line boundaries, leading to asymmetric margins and overflow glitches ("digitized, but without layout").

docs.title: 4.2 The Solution: The 3 Pillars of Dual-Path Architecture
docs.text:
1. Path 1: The Facsimile Guarantee (*.perfect_sandwich.pdf)
  2. High-resolution scans remain 100% intact as pixel-perfect background images.
  3. Searchable OCR text is overlaid via PDF Text Rendering Mode 3 (neither fill nor stroke text) on exact bounding box coordinates.

  4. Guarantee: 100% original layout, zero typographical risk, complete archival citation fidelity.

  5. Path 2: Universal Canonical Ground-Truth Alignment (scripts/align_canonical.py)

  6. Instead of blindly guessing scan geometry, raw OCR text is synchronized via sequence tracking and fuzzy matching against canonical reference databases (e.g. 3,997 Sūtras in sutras.json or 2,259 roots in dhatupatha_canonical.json).
  7. OCR errors on damaged 19th-century lead types are automatically repaired, gaps audited, and the work consolidated into an archival master JSON.

  8. Library stamps, scan bars, and rogue script drift (Hebrew/Telugu noise on fine Sanskrit diacritics) are cleanly eliminated via declarative heuristics (strip_library_boilerplates, strip_rogue_scripts).

  9. Path 3: Direct IIIF Ingestion & Facsimile Linking (scripts/import_iiif.py)

  10. Native ingestion of digital collections across IIIF Presentation API v2 and v3 endpoints (UB Heidelberg, British Library, BnF Gallica, BSB München).
  11. Direct linking of all edition page breaks in TEI-P5 XML (<pb n="..." facs="..."/>) with canonical IIIF image URIs.

  12. Declarative configuration via job.config.json (iiif_manifest, iiif_template).

  13. Layout Fidelity Through Section-Aware Typography

  14. Avoid enforcing a rigid global 2-column layout across the entire book:
    • Front Matter (Preface, Introduction): Single-column continuous prose with original paragraphs and scan page margin links ([S. 6]).
    • Main Body (Dictionary/Tables): Two-column dictionary layout with vertical column rules (grid.vline) and centered colophons (typeset_mode: dictionary_grid).
    • Back Matter (Indices/Appendices): Structure matching historical registers.
    • Hermetic Font Vendoring: Local OpenType font bundling via --font-path (prioritizing Noto Serif Devanagari and Linux Libertine O).

docs.title: 5. Standard Directory Layout per Book
docs.text:
Every work processed by AlexandriaSandwich generates the following standardized file structure:

output/books/<book_id>/
├── <book_id>.sandwich.pdf          # 1:1 Facsimile + Tesseract text layer
├── <book_id>.perfect_sandwich.pdf  # Restored facsimile + optimized Mistral text layer
├── <book_id>.typeset_edition.pdf   # Semantic vector edition via Typst (Böhtlingk standard)
├── <book_id>.digital.pdf           # 1:1 Page-concordance digital PDF
├── <book_id>.epub                  # Reflowable eBook with embedded fonts
├── <book_id>.tei.xml               # TEI-P5 Archival XML
├── book.json                       # Complete semantic syntax tree (AST)
└── book.md                         # Consolidated UTF-8 Markdown text

docs.title: 1. Objective & Core Concept
docs.text:
AlexandriaSandwich automates high-quality digitization of books and archival documents into long-term archival formats and modern digital representations.

A Sandwich PDF consists of two precisely registered layers: 1. Visual Image Layer (top): The original cleaned scan image is preserved 1:1 down to the pixel. No destructive typesetting or visual replacement occurs. 2. Invisible Text Layer (bottom): An invisible vector text layer (GlyphLessFont) with bounding boxes that enables full-text search, selection, and copy-paste.

The pipeline follows a Local-First approach with AI Fallback: regular scans are processed locally and cost-effectively; cloud-based AI is engaged only when local OCR confidence degrades.

docs.title: Case Study: Bṛhadāraṇyaka-Upaniṣad I.4 (Synoptic Edition)
docs.text:
Multilateral philological alignment of three textual witnesses (Devanagari, IAST, 2 German translations) into a 33-page synoptic edition and interactive QA viewer.

🔗 Project Repository: github.com/birchville-org/brhadaranyaka

docs.title: 1. Context & Challenge
docs.text:
Unlike standard unilinear book digitization (scanned pages => sandwich PDF), reading Bṛhadāraṇyaka-Upaniṣad I.4 (Mādhyandina recension: The Ur-Subject and creation myth) required the synoptic synchronization of three disparate sources:

  1. Canonical Sanskrit Text: Scholarly IAST transliteration by Anna Esposito.
  2. Walter Slaje (2009): Upanischaden: Arkanum des Veda (Insel Verlag) offering modern philosophical translation, terminology (Ursubjekt), and a 36-entry philological commentary.
  3. Otto von Böhtlingk (1889): Bṛhadāraṇjakopanishad in der Mādhyandina-Recension (St. Petersburg) providing the historical critical edition and notes.

docs.title: 2. Implementation Steps
docs.text:
1. Multimodal AI OCR (mistral-ocr-latest):
  2. Extracted Böhtlingk 1889 (12 pages) and Slaje 2009 (15 pages).
  3. Structured translation pages (pp. 108–117) and philological commentary (pp. 482–493).
  4. Canonical Alignment:
  5. Aligned all sources across 31 semantic sections (1.4.1 to 1.4.31).
  6. Generated ligature-safe Devanagari with danda formatting.
  7. Repository Decoupling:
  8. Following the boethlingk model, all artifacts were transferred to the dedicated repository birchville-org/brhadaranyaka.

docs.title: 3. Output Formats in the Edition Repository
docs.text:
• QA Viewer (viewer.html): Interactive split-pane editor adhering to the Payer Global Web Editor Standard with silent auto-repair and diacritics bar.
  • Restored Facsimile Sandwich (slaje2009.perfect_sandwich.pdf): 15-page high-end facsimile (2.28 MB) with Content-Aware Margin Masking via AlexandriaSandwich v1.7.0.
  • Typeset PDF (brhadaranyaka_1_4_synopsis.pdf): 33-page scholarly publication via WeasyPrint.
  • TEI-P5 XML (brhadaranyaka_1_4.tei.xml): Standard archival format with parallel alignment.
  • EPUB 3 (brhadaranyaka_1_4.epub): Reflowable eBook with embedded fonts (Noto Serif Devanagari & Linux Libertine O).
  • Master JSON (brhadaranyaka_1_4_master.json): Single Source of Truth AST.
  • Release: Compiled and published live as brhadaranyaka v1.1.0.

docs.title: Case Study & Architecture: Dhātu-Pāṭha (Böhtlingk Standard)
docs.text: Canonical ground truth, bilingual facing-page alignment pipeline, and hybrid Typst vector typesetting for 2,259 verbal roots across 410 book pages. 🔗 Project Repository: github.com/birchville-org/dhatupatha 🌐 Live QA Viewer: birchville-org.github.io/dhatupatha

docs.title: 1.1 The Phenomenon: "Digitized without layout" vs. "Digitized AND original layout"
docs.text:
During the initial digitization of the Dhātu-Pāṭha (Pāṇinian catalog of verbal roots), a fundamental discrepancy became evident: * The reference project Otto von Böhtlingk (1887) produced an output combining complete layout fidelity with sharp typography ("digitized AND original layout"). * In contrast, an early direct OCR-to-typeset attempt on Dhātu-Pāṭha resulted in an unstructured stream: two-column root listings collapsed, and meanings merged awkwardly into paragraphs ("digitized, but without layout").

Resolving this discrepancy and transferring the Böhtlingk Standard to the Dhātu-Pāṭha established core architectural insights for the entire AlexandriaSandwich pipeline.

docs.title: 1.2 Structure of the Historical Source
docs.text: The 410-page volume features a complex two-fold internal organization: 1. Section Hierarchy: * Front Matter (pp. 1–25): Continuous single-column prose (preface, grammatical introduction, phonetic rules) structured into cohesive paragraphs. * Main Matter (pp. 26–285): Rigorous two-column dictionary grid across the 10 Gaṇas (root classes from Bhvādi to Curādi). * Back Matter (pp. 286–410): Alphabetic indices, concordance tables, and appendices. 2. Bilingual Facing Pages: * Odd Pages (Right): Primary Sanskrit text in Devanāgarī with traditional Aupadeśika markers and locative meanings (arthas). * Even Pages (Left): Facing scholarly transliteration (IAST) with English translations and grammatical tags.

docs.title: 2. Root Cause Analysis: Why Blind "Reverse-Layout" Fails
docs.text:
Attempting to mathematically or heuristically reverse-engineer the original layout directly from raw, sequential OCR text fails due to two structural barriers:

[Raw OCR Data Stream] ──► Sequential Extraction (1D)
                                  │
         ┌────────────────────────┴────────────────────────┐
         ▼                                                 ▼
[Problem 1: Serialization Loss]                  [Problem 2: Layout Constraint]
2D tabular root/meaning alignment                A global 2-column rule destroys
collapses into flat 1D paragraphs.               the single-column preface;
Typst must guess column breaks.                  1-column destroys the lexicon.
  1. Serialization Loss: OCR engines (both Tesseract and multimodal VLMs) process text blocks sequentially. In multi-column lexicons, roots and their respective translations become interleaved or broken across lines.
  2. Blanket Layout Constraints: Imposing a rigid global column count across an entire volume either squeezes the prose preface into unreadable narrow columns or dissolves the dictionary's tabular structure into an unstructured list.

docs.title: 3. The Solution: The 4-Pillar Böhtlingk Standard
docs.text:
AlexandriaSandwich strictly decouples archival facsimile preservation from semantically driven vector typesetting:

                              ┌──────────────────────┐
                              │     Raw Scans        │
                              └──────────┬───────────┘
                                         │
                 ┌───────────────────────┴───────────────────────┐
                 ▼                                               ▼
   [ PILLAR 1: FACSIMILE GUARANTEE ]              [ PILLAR 2: CANONICAL ALIGNMENT ]
   • 1:1 untouched scan pixels                    • Fuzzy match vs dhatupatha_canonical.json
   • Invisible bbox text layer                    • Bilingual 10-Gaṇa state machine
   • Dhatu-patha.perfect_sandwich.pdf             • 100% gapless dhatupatha_complete.json
                                                                 │
                                                                 ▼
   [ PILLAR 4: HERMETIC FONT DEPLOY ]             [ PILLAR 3: TYPST VECTOR EDITION ]
   • data/fonts/ (Noto + Libertine)               • pp. 1–25:  1-column continuous prose
   • APT fonts-noto-extra on Linux                • pp. 26–285: 2-column grid + grid.vline
   • Zero tofu question marks (?)                 • Marginal concordance: [S. 26]

docs.title: Pillar 1: The Facsimile Guarantee (*.perfect_sandwich.pdf)
docs.text:
• The 410 original high-resolution scans remain visually untouched at 1:1 pixel fidelity.
  • Corrected OCR text is embedded invisibly (PDF Text Rendering Mode 3) precisely along the bounding boxes of historical print lines.
  • Guarantee: 100% archival authenticity, zero layout hallucination risk, instantaneous full-text search.

docs.title: Pillar 2: Canonical Ground Truth & Bilingual Facing-Page Alignment
docs.text: Rather than typesetting uncurated OCR output, the text is structured through a two-step alignment pipeline: 1. Canonical Ground-Truth Database (scripts/build_dhatupatha_groundtruth.py): * Generates data/dhatupatha_canonical.json (2,259 roots across all 10 Gaṇas). * Contains canonical Devanāgarī, IAST, Aupadeśika markers (e.g., टु, डु, इर्), Sanskrit locative arthas (भू सत्तायाम्), English translations, and Pāṇinian classifications (Svarita-Anudātta, Sakarmaka/Akarmaka, Seṭ/Aniṭ). 2. Bilingual Facing-Page Alignment Engine (scripts/align_dhatupatha.py): * Leveraging the facing-page layout (odd pages Devanāgarī, even pages IAST), the 10-Gaṇa state machine matches OCR candidates against both scripts simultaneously. * Ambiguous or damaged Devanāgarī lead types are validated against the Romanized transliteration on the facing page, and vice versa. * Result: data/dhatupatha_complete.json (100% gapless master catalog linked to original scan page numbers).

docs.title: Pillar 3: Section-Specific Layout Fidelity in Typst (scripts/build_typeset_edition.py)
docs.text: The vector edition dynamically shifts its typography to honor the book's logical sections: * Front Matter (pp. 1–25): * Single-column continuous prose with generous margins. * Preserves historical paragraph divisions and section markers. * Marginal references link back to original scan pages ([S. 6], [S. 11]). * Main Matter / Dictionary (pp. 26–285): * Two-column dictionary grid separated by a vertical rule (grid.vline). * Centered Gaṇa headings (e.g., 1. Bhvādigaṇaḥ / भ्वादिगणः). * Bold Devanāgarī roots with accents, accompanied by italic IAST, locative meanings, and English translations. * Marginal navigation anchors ([S. 26]). * Running Headers: * Dynamic Typst headers in code mode: Even pages display the book title; odd pages display the current Gaṇa name and page counter.

docs.title: Pillar 4: Cross-Platform Font Vendoring & Linux Tofu Fix
docs.text:
A critical issue identified when moving from macOS development to headless Linux servers (alex.local, Docker): * The Problem: Typst rendered cleanly on macOS because macOS provides system fonts for Indic scripts (Devanagari MT, Kohinoor Devanagari, Baskerville). However, inside the Linux worker container (Ubuntu 24.04), all Devanāgarī characters rendered as question marks inside boxes (?, tofu). * The Root Cause: 1. In Ubuntu 24.04, fonts-noto-core does NOT contain Indic scripts. 2. Typst searches system directories by default and fails to locate Indic glyphs. * The Solution: 1. Hermetic Font Vendoring: Storing OpenType/TrueType master fonts directly inside the repository under data/fonts/: * NotoSerifDevanagari-Regular.ttf & NotoSerifDevanagari-Bold.ttf * LinLibertine_R.otf, LinLibertine_RB.otf, LinLibertine_RI.otf 2. Automatic Font Path: Passing --font-path data/fonts to every Typst invocation. 3. Universal Font Cascade: 

#set text(
  font: ("Linux Libertine O", "Baskerville", "Times New Roman", "Noto Serif Devanagari", "Devanagari MT", "Kohinoor Devanagari", "Noto Sans Devanagari"),
  size: 10pt,
  lang: "de"
)
4. Container Packages: Installing fonts-noto-extra (APT) and pymupdf (PIP) in the worker image.

docs.text: To guarantee automated execution on Linux workers (alex.local, Synology, Debian/Ubuntu) without manual intervention, configure:

# System fonts including Indic script coverage
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \

    fonts-noto-extra \
    fonts-linuxlibertine \
    fonts-dejavu-core \

    pymupdf \

    lxml

The master bash script automatically detects aligned canonical datasets: 

if [ -f "data/dhatupatha_complete.json" ]; then
    echo "==> Generating typographical vector edition via Typst..."
    python3 scripts/build_typeset_edition.py \
        --input data/dhatupatha_complete.json \
        --output data/output/pdf/Dhatu-patha.typeset_edition.pdf
fi

docs.title: 6. Summary Conclusion
docs.text: Production-grade fidelity is not achieved by attempting to "reverse-guess" layout from unstructured OCR text. It requires two distinct, complementary workflows: 1. The Sandwich PDF preserves historical authenticity and archival citation integrity at 1:1 pixel fidelity. 2. The Typst Vector Edition leverages canonical ground truth to build a publication-grade edition honoring original section-specific layout conventions.

docs.title: Case Study & Pipeline Architecture: Pāṇini's Grammar (Otto von Böhtlingk, 1887)
docs.text:
Complete historical digitization, canonical alignment, and generation of searchable Sandwich material for 3,997 Sūtras across 478 book pages.

🔗 Project Repository: github.com/birchville-org/boethlingk

docs.title: 1.1 Source Work
docs.text: Otto von Böhtlingk's edition Pâṇini's Grammatik, herausgegeben, übersetzt, erläutert und mit verschiedenen Indices versehen (Leipzig, H. Haessel, 1887) is the preeminent global philological reference work for the ancient Indian grammatical system of the Aṣṭādhyāyī.

docs.title: 1.2 Philological & Typographical Challenge
docs.text:
The work combines three disparate scripts and languages in tight physical proximity: 1. Sanskrit in Devanagari: Complex 19th-century movable lead type with historical ligatures, conjunct consonants, and Virāmas. 2. German in historical Antiqua: Scholarly translation and grammatical commentary with era-specific typography. 3. Scientific Transliteration (IAST): Latin alphabet with numerous combining diacritics (ā, ī, ū, ṛ, ṝ, ḷ, ḹ, ṃ, ḥ, ṅ, ñ, ṭ, ḍ, ṇ, ś, ṣ) and accent marks (Udātta, Svarita).

Conventional local OCR engines (Tesseract, Kraken, ABBYY) fail on this polyglossic layout with prohibitive error rates and script confusion.

docs.title: 1.3 Digitization Goal
docs.text: The objective is the production of a multi-tiered, archive-grade digital corpus: 1. 1:1 Sandwich PDF: Visually pristine, high-resolution original scans from Heidelberg University Library (pixel-preserved) with an invisible, geometrically registered full-text layer. 2. Structured Single Source of Truth (Master JSON): Exhaustive decomposition of the entire work into structured Sūtra objects (Sūtra number, canonical Devanagari, IAST, German translation, grammatical commentary, book page index). 3. Standalone QA Viewer: A lightweight web application following the Payer Global Web Editor Standard for visual verification and correction with split-pane view and Silent Auto-Repair. 4. TEI-XML Foundation: A standardized corpus conforming to Text Encoding Initiative (TEI-P5) for digital humanities and philological editions.

docs.title: 2. Implemented End-to-End Pipeline
docs.text:
[Heidelberg University Facsimiles] 
       │ (Pages 1 to 478, JPG)
       ▼
[Step 1: Local Image Caching] ───────► data/img_cache/7_3A000000XXX_...jpg
       │
       ▼
[Step 2: Multimodal AI OCR] ─────────► mistral-ocr-latest (Mistral Python SDK)
       │                               ├── data/mistral/*.mistral.md   (Layout Markdown)
       │                               └── data/mistral/*.mistral.json (Bounding Box Geometry)
       ▼
[Step 3: Canonical Alignment] ───────► scripts/align_mistral_sutras.py
       │                               ├── Heuristic Sūtra segmentation (#, ##, ॥...॥)
       │                               ├── SequenceMatcher alignment against data/sutras.json
       │                               ├── 4-Pāda-per-Adhyāya state machine
       │                               └── Colophon and noise filtering
       ▼
[Step 4: Consolidation] ─────────────► data/ashtadhyayi_complete_boethlingk1887.json
       │                               (3,997 Sūtras = 100.0% coverage & 0 duplicates)

docs.title: Conclusion & Architectural Decision:
docs.text:
• Mistral OCR: Gold standard for historical Indic scripts and bulk processing (highest ligature accuracy, minimal latency).
  • Qwen2.5-VL 8-bit (Local): Robust, privacy-preserving alternative for modern and European typography (99.96% accuracy). 8-bit quantization reduces inference latency by 33% with negligible character loss (-0.2%).

docs.title: Step 3: Canonical Alignment & Heuristics (scripts/align_mistral_sutras.py)
docs.text:
• Fuzzy Canonical Matching: When OCR misreads a Sūtra counter (e.g. reading Devanagari digit ८ as ६: ६५ instead of ८५), a SequenceMatcher algorithm compares normalized Sanskrit text with expected Sūtras in data/sutras.json. At similarity >= 0.45, the counter is automatically adjusted.
  • Compensated Token Length: Extremely long Sanskrit compounds (e.g. Sūtra 5.4.77 with 185 characters lacking a leading #) are reliably identified via Danda patterns (॥...॥) up to 350 characters.
  • Pāda and Adhyāya Rollover: Because the Aṣṭādhyāyī strictly consists of 8 Adhyāyas with exactly 4 Pādas each, the state machine triggers an automatic increment after Pāda 4 (state["adhyaya"] += 1, state["pada"] = 1), even when printed colophons are broken or omitted.
  • Foreign Script Filtering: Stray glyphs (e.g., stray Telugu or Hebrew artifacts caused by damaged metal types) are filtered prior to consolidation.
  • Addenda Isolation: Content following concluding Sūtra 8.4.68 (अ अ) (Böhtlingk's Nachträge und Verbesserungen) is partitioned into separate addenda objects, preventing commentary pollution.

docs.title: 5. Sandwich PDF Assembly in AlexandriaSandwich (v1.7.0 Pipeline)
docs.text: The completed Sandwich PDF and re-typeset editions were assembled via the AlexandriaSandwich machinery: * Cleaned Facsimile (Content-Aware Perfect Sandwich): data/output/boehtlingk1887.perfect_sandwich.pdf (248.85 MB, 478 pages) - Complete elimination of gutter shadows, binding stripes, and scanner edge artifacts via dynamic Content-Aware Margin Masking. - 1:1 pixel fidelity of the historical 1887 print with pure #FFFFFF background leveling. * Standard Facsimile: data/output/boehtlingk1887_sandwich.pdf (278.16 MB, 478 pages) * Invisible Text Layer: Using PDF Text Rendering Mode 3 (Neither fill nor stroke text) and unicode font mapping (Identity-H), 14,267 text fragments are placed at their exact pixel coordinates. * Modernized Typeset Edition v2: data/output/boethlingk1887_typeset_edition_v2.pdf (7.62 MB, Typst vector typography per Scholarly Synthesis) with 47 hierarchical bookmarks and native page label injection. * Release: Compiled and published live as boethlingk v1.5.0. * Result: Reading presents the authentic historical facsimile of 1887 in pristine restored condition. Text selection, copy-paste, and full-text search (Devanagari, IAST, German) interact directly with precise underlying vector coordinates.

docs.title: 6. Scholarly TEI-P5 Edition
docs.text: For archival preservation and digital humanities interoperability: * Target File: data/tei/boehtlingk1887_p5.xml (2.90 MB) * Validation: 100% schema-valid against TEI All RelaxNG (schemas/tei_all.rng). * Structure: 3,997 <tei:entry> elements, 478 <tei:pb> page breaks linked to Heidelberg IIIF facsimile URLs, 8 Adhyāya and 32 Pāda sections, and 50 corrigenda items in <back>.

docs.title: 7. QA Viewer (Payer Global Web Editor Standard)
docs.text: For editorial review and long-term curation, viewer.html was implemented: * Split-Pane: Left pane provides responsive zoom & pan of original scans; right pane provides the Sūtra editor. * Snippet Toolbar: Instant insertion of Dandas (॥, ।, ऽ, °), IAST diacritics, and philological notations (∠±, ∠_, v. l., Kāç., RV.). * Silent Auto-Repair on Save: On save (⌘S), ASCII pipes (||) silently convert to Dandas (॥), whitespace is normalized, and noise characters are stripped. Visual confirmation is indicated by button color pulses (Yellow = Auto-Repair, Green = Saved). * Local Storage First & Export: Saves working revisions locally in browser storage and enables direct saving to disk via File System Access API (showSaveFilePicker).
